sources_considered.why: Primary CBRE H1 2026 data on how much capacity under construction is preleased.
Industry piece dated June 2026 describing spec AI campuses built before tenants sign, with named examples.
Describes who signs long-term GPU offtakes: AI labs, often backstopped by hyperscalers.

receipt.public_excerpt: More than 80% of all capacity under construction is already preleased, up from 74.3% a year ago. This leaves less than 1,500 MW available for pre-leasing across North America's primary markets.

evidence_items.explanation: Close to a fifth of capacity under construction in the main North American markets (up to about 1,500 MW) had no tenant in H1 2026. So not all capacity being built has locked-in demand. Most of it does, though, and the share is rising.

evidence_items.locator: section The Projects That Illustrate the Model

receipt.public_excerpt: Applied Digital's Delta Forge 1 campus in Boyce, Louisiana represents the spec build at scale: .6 billion, 300 acres, announced as AI campus infrastructure ahead of named tenants. CloudBurst Data Centers broke ground on a 1.2 GW campus in Central Texas without disclosed pre-leasing.

evidence_items.explanation: Names large AI campuses being built before any tenant was named or any preleasing disclosed. These are AI data centers without locked-in customer demand.

receipt.public_excerpt: It is also common to see Hyperscalers backstop these deals – serving as the direct offtaker from these Neoclouds but then on-selling the compute to an AI Lab.

evidence_items.explanation: Says long-term offtakes are dominated by AI labs, often backstopped by hyperscalers. This fits his description of where locked-in demand comes from, but it is background, not proof of an exhaustive list.

unresolved_gaps: CBRE figures cover all data centers in eight primary North American markets, not only AI facilities, and not global capacity.

No complete public register of AI data center tenants exists. Other committed customers (for example Oracle or Nvidia under backstop deals) may exist outside his list. Because he limited the list to what he could find, this is not scored.
